commit.message:
feat(doctrine-v3): MoralGrounding + MeasurabilityHonesty theorems (zero sorry) (#12)

* feat(doctrine-v3): MoralGrounding + MeasurabilityHonesty theorems (zero sorry)

Add two fully-discharged Lean 4 theorems under Lutar/DoctrineV3/:

  - LutarLean.MoralGroundingTheorem (§6 Moral Grounding Theorem)
  - LutarLean.MeasurabilityHonestyTheorem (§7 Measurability Honesty Theorem)

Both theorems carry ZERO sorry, ZERO admit, ZERO new axiom declarations.
Proofs proceed by structural case analysis over finite inductive types
(HarmCategory with 6 constructors; ReceiptSlot with 2 constructors).

Formalization choice: the structural core of each doctrine theorem is
encoded (finite conjunction decomposition for P_moral; two-constructor
partition for receipt slots). The probabilistic components (A₇ ≥ 0.95,
A₉ ≥ 0.95) are scoped out as they require a probability-space axiom not
present in Mathlib without extension.

ORCID: 0009-0001-0110-4173
Author: Stephen P. Lutar Jr. <stephen@szlholdings.com>
Doctrine V3 §6 / §7

* fix(doctrine-v3): drop deriving Repr on Output struct

Function-typed fields (HarmCategory → Bool) have no canonical Repr
instance in Lean 4. Removing the auto-derive — the proof does not
require Repr; only DecidableEq extensibility (via funext) is needed.

Per Doctrine V3 §6: zero sorry, zero admit, zero new axioms.
No bandaid: the function-typed decision procedure is the intentional
design choice so the proof is stable under H-extension.

Signed-off-by: Stephen P. Lutar Jr. <stephen@szlholdings.com>

* fix(doctrine): replace 'Jr.' with canonical byline 'Lutar, Stephen P.'

DOCTRINE FIX: Copyright headers in MoralGrounding.lean, MeasurabilityHonesty.lean,
and Axioms.lean used 'Stephen P. Lutar Jr.' — forbidden pattern.
Corrected to canonical form: 'Lutar, Stephen P.'

Doctrine sweep: PASS (0 violations after fix)

Byline: Lutar, Stephen P. · ORCID 0009-0001-0110-4173 · SZL Holdings
Co-authored-by: PM-Overwatch <stephen@szlholdings.com>

commit.message:
chore(repo): Series A hygiene — LICENSE, SECURITY, CITATION.cff, CODEOWNERS, Scorecard hardening (#9)

Brings lutar-lean up to the same Series-A baseline as ouroboros and ouroboros-thesis.

Repo hygiene (new files):
- LICENSE (Apache-2.0)
- SECURITY.md (disclosure policy)
- CONTRIBUTING.md (org template)
- CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant 2.1)
- CITATION.cff (Lean formalization software citation, linked to v9 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20053148)
- .zenodo.json (so GitHub Releases auto-mint a Zenodo DOI for the Lean proof)
- .github/CODEOWNERS

Workflow hardening (addresses Scorecard findings):
- .github/workflows/lean.yml:
  * Add top-level 'permissions: {}' (Token-Permissions)
  * Pin actions/checkout, leanprover/lean-action, step-security/harden-runner by SHA (Pinned-Dependencies)
  * Add 'persist-credentials: false' on checkout
  * Add step-security/harden-runner (egress audit)
- .github/workflows/scorecard.yml: reuse org-wide reusable workflow
- .github/dependabot.yml: per-repo GitHub Actions weekly updates

No code changes — Lean library and executables untouched.

Co-authored-by: Stephen P. Lutar Jr. <stephen@szlholdings.com>

commit.message:
fix(lean): Mathlib v4.13.0 API compatibility — restore green build (#7)

* fix(lean): Mathlib v4.13.0 API compatibility

- Pin Mathlib to v4.13.0 in lakefile
- Update BigOperators import path (split in v4.13)
- Fix Finset.sup'/inf' Nonempty witness shape (takes Finset.Nonempty directly)
- Egyptian.lean: simp only + field_simp pattern
- Axioms.lean: IsBounded takes hk : 0 < k for non-empty fiber

Builds clean on Lean 4 + Mathlib v4.13.0.

Signed-off-by: Stephen P. Lutar Jr. <stephen@szlholdings.com>

* ci(lean): generate lake-manifest.json before lean-action configure

lean-action's configure step refuses to proceed without lake-manifest.json
on disk. The repo .gitignore excludes /.lake and other build artifacts,
but does not commit the manifest — so CI needs to generate it.

Install elan first, run `lake update -R` to fetch dependencies and write
the manifest, then hand off to lean-action for the cached Mathlib build.

Signed-off-by: Stephen P. Lutar Jr. <stephen@szlholdings.com>

* fix(lean): move module imports above doc comment in Lutar.lean

Lean 4 requires 'import' statements to come before any non-import tokens at the top of the file. The /-! ... -/ module doc was triggering 'invalid import command' on CI.

This moves the doc comment below the imports while preserving the documentation content.

* fix(lean): remove invalid escape in Main.lean string

Lean 4 string interpolation with s! treats backslash-brace as an invalid escape sequence. Replaced the unicode-decorated interpolated string with a plain ASCII string. Output text is purely informational so this doesn't affect any theorem.

* fix(lean): declare RefVectors as lean_lib so MainRef can import it

The 'Run reference-vectors parity check' CI step builds 'lake exe ref_vectors' whose root MainRef.lean imports a top-level RefVectors module. Without a lean_lib declaration, lake doesn't compile RefVectors.lean, so the executable fails with 'unknown module prefix RefVectors'.

Adding 'lean_lib RefVectors' with roots := #[`RefVectors] makes lake build the top-level RefVectors.lean as its own library, which resolves the import.

* fix(lean): move imports above doc comment in RefVectors.lean

Same Lean 4 strictness as Lutar.lean — module-level imports must precede the /-! ... -/ module doc comment, otherwise the kernel emits 'invalid import command'. Reordered with imports at the top followed by the unchanged documentation block.

---------

Signed-off-by: Stephen P. Lutar Jr. <stephen@szlholdings.com>
Co-authored-by: Stephen P. Lutar Jr. <stephen@szlholdings.com>

commit.message:
feat(ref-vectors): cross-runtime Λ₉ parity check (lake exe ref_vectors)

- New: RefVectors.lean (parses TS-generated reference-vectors.json,
  computes Λ₉ via Float, checks tolerance against the stored value).
- New: MainRef.lean (executable entry point).
- New: reference-vectors.json (10 golden vectors, generated from
  @workspace/ouroboros-invariant lutarInvariant9 in the platform
  monorepo at commit 0c2229f31).
- lakefile.lean: register lean_exe `ref_vectors`.
- .github/workflows/lean.yml: run `lake exe ref_vectors reference-vectors.json`
  on every push, asserting the Lean Float implementation agrees with the
  TS implementation on every golden vector (abs=1e-12, rel=1e-9).

Important caveat documented in RefVectors.lean: Float arithmetic is NOT
kernel-verified — it is trusted at the level of Lean's Float builtin.
The mathematical correctness of Λ_k(x) = (∏ xᵢ)^(1/k) lives in
Lutar/Invariant.lean (kernel-verified). This file checks operational
parity between the two implementations on a curated set of inputs.
